reference_title: Design and Construction of Continuous Flight Auger Piles

sections.title: Purpose
sections.summary: GEC-8 is a state-of-the-practice manual for the design and construction of continuous flight auger (CFA) piles, including augered cast-in-place (ACIP), drilled displacement (DD) and screw piles. It presents an Allowable Stress Design (ASD) procedure because resistance factors had not yet been calibrated for CFA piles for LRFD.
sections.body: The document develops a state-of-the-practice manual for the design and construction of continuous flight auger (CFA) piles, including piles commonly referred to as augered cast-in-place (ACIP) piles, drilled displacement (DD) piles and screw piles. An Allowable Stress Design (ASD) procedure is presented because resistance (strength reduction) factors have not yet been calibrated for CFA piles for a Load Resistance Factored Design (LRFD) approach. The intended audience is engineers and construction specialists involved in the design, construction and contracting of foundation elements for transportation structures. (p. 1)
key_points: CFA piles include ACIP, drilled displacement (DD) and screw piles (p. 1).
Design is presented as ASD; resistance factors for LRFD had not been calibrated for CFA piles (p. 1).
sections.applicability: General purpose and scope of FHWA GEC-8 CFA pile design and construction manual

sections.title: Background
sections.summary: CFA piles had seldom been used for U.S. transportation structures because of perceived quality-control difficulties and the fit of a proprietary technology to design-bid-build. Automated monitoring now supports a performance-based approach: the contractor carries more responsibility, verified by full-scale load tests and monitored installation parameters.
sections.body: CFA piles have been used worldwide and in the U.S. commercial market but not frequently for transportation structures in the United States, because of perceived difficulties in quality control and in incorporating a rapidly developing (often proprietary) technology into the prescriptive design-bid-build concept. Automated monitoring and recording devices alleviate the quality-control concerns and support performance-based contracting. In the performance-based approach the specialty contractor or design-build team has greater freedom and greater responsibility for foundation performance; instead of rigorous prescriptive specifications, a comprehensive testing program verifies performance. Full-scale load tests verify load carrying capability; automatic monitoring during construction of test and production piles establishes the construction parameters (down-force, torque, grout take) and verifies they are met for every production pile; load tests may also be performed on production piles selected by the owner. The document covers pile types, materials, equipment and procedures, QC/QA, a performance specification adaptable to projects, methods for static axial capacity of single piles with a comparison of U.S. and European methods, group effects on axial capacity and settlement, lateral capacity of single piles and groups, and a step-by-step selection and design method. (p. 1)
key_points: Performance-based approach: comprehensive testing program instead of prescriptive specifications (p. 1).
Automatic monitoring establishes down-force, torque and grout take and verifies them for every production pile (p. 1).
Full-scale load tests may be performed on production piles selected by the owner (p. 1).
sections.applicability: Rationale for performance-based approach to CFA pile specification in transportation projects

sections.title: Relevant Publications
sections.summary: Chapter 9 lists the references used in developing the manual, including key publications on the design of augered pile foundations and existing FHWA and AASHTO publications on engineering principles related to CFA piles.
sections.body: A list of the references used in the development of the manual is presented in Chapter 9. They include key publications on the design of augered pile foundations and existing Federal Highway Administration and AASHTO publications that include engineering principles related to CFA piles. (p. 2)

sections.title: Document Organization
sections.summary: Organization: Ch 2 pile types and basic mechanisms; Ch 3 applications for transportation projects; Ch 4 construction techniques and materials; Ch 5 static capacity methods (U.S. and European); Ch 6 step-by-step design with an annotated example; Ch 7 QC/QA; Ch 8 guide performance specification; Ch 9 references; Appendix A method comparisons; Appendix B spreadsheet solutions.
sections.body: The document is organized as follows: Chapter 2, description of CFA pile types and basic mechanisms (main system components, typical equipment, construction sequence); Chapter 3, applications for transportation projects (advantages and limitations, favorable and unfavorable project and geotechnical conditions); Chapter 4, construction techniques, materials and recommended practice; Chapter 5, evaluation and comparison of U.S. and European methods for the static capacity of CFA piles; Chapter 6, a step-by-step generalized method for selection and design, with an annotated example; Chapter 7, QC/QA procedures and automated QC/QA equipment; Chapter 8, guide construction specifications (a performance specification); Chapter 9, references; Appendix A, comparisons of methods for estimating the static axial capacity of CFA piles; Appendix B, spreadsheet solutions for axial capacity of single CFA piles. (p. 2)
key_points: Chapter 5 gives the capacity methods; Chapter 6 the step-by-step design with an example (p. 2).
Appendix A compares capacity methods; Appendix B gives spreadsheet solutions (p. 2).
sections.applicability: Organization guide for GEC-8 chapters and appendices
